subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should memoryFlush and preflight compaction be moved off the foreground session lane, or should OpenClaw keep in-lane compaction with bounded timeouts and watchdog recovery?
rationale: Both current code and the latest release still serialize compaction with foreground session work, but changing that contract affects session consistency, transcript checkpoints, cancellation, and delivery ordering.

options.title: Isolate compaction work
options.body: Move memoryFlush/preflight compaction onto a dedicated or preemptible background lane while preserving session checkpoint safety and foreground delivery ordering.

options.title: Keep in-lane with recovery
options.body: Treat the 180s timeout plus stuck-session abort recovery as the intended behavior and document that foreground turns may wait during compaction.

options.title: Split narrower fixes
options.body: Track memoryFlush escalation, compaction cancellation, and overflow truncation separately while leaving this broader lane-isolation behavior unresolved.

recommendation.title: Isolate compaction work
recommendation.body: Move memoryFlush/preflight compaction onto a dedicated or preemptible background lane while preserving session checkpoint safety and foreground delivery ordering.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history and current shallow blame put steipete closest to the embedded-run, compaction, and queue surfaces that need the product decision.
